## Context / Problem
Plan-review Pass 1 owns mature chunk sizing, model ladders, cache warming, bounded concurrency, container/prerequisite stages, cancellation, and resumable checkpoints. Its current result shape can nevertheless collapse a failed criterion to an empty success and checkpoint it, and its checkpoint identity omits policy, prompt, contract, and topology inputs. RP-06 must obtain trustworthy partial results without losing these operational lessons.

## Approach
Add a plan-review strategy adapter that compiles the current Round-A discovery topology into `DiscoveryStagePlan` units from the S1 `CriteriaSnapshot`, then executes through the S2 shared kernel. Preserve the existing plan-review YAML/BPMN graph, facet packing, one-criterion fallback, model ladder, centrality-derived default cap, explicit override semantics, bounded concurrency, cache warming, container/prerequisite calls, and live cancellation checks.

Project criteria use the effective snapshot once. Disabled or non-applicable entries produce stored skip provenance and no calls. The gate persists the versioned safe discovery trace and new digest-complete success-only checkpoint envelopes in its reducer-ignored review journal. The key includes plan material, code/ref, criteria snapshot, prompt/contract, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and namespace version. Legacy checkpoints are ignored rather than translated; failed, cancelled, skipped, and budget-shed work remains missing.

Apply the approved final failure policy after RP-01 exhausts a local operation: preserve successful findings and continue independent units; skip dependents of missing work; return unsigned `INDETERMINATE` for missing blocking-capable coverage unless a real blocking finding wins `BLOCK`; allow advisory-only gaps to pass. Keep deterministic-floor, systemic provider/configuration, whole-tier, cancellation, relation-snapshot, and signing behavior unchanged. The normal review result and `review-plan --status` remain narrow end-result contracts with no per-unit trace.

Use one-call-set shadow comparison during migration. The legacy projection remains available only to compare/rollback; it may not write checkpoints or become the final verdict. No duplicate LLM calls and no new operator configuration flag are introduced.

## Testing
Use real workflow-to-runner contract tests and stateful fault injection at the model-call/checkpoint-write boundaries. Oracles assert final verdict, exact call set/order, usage, new journal bytes, checkpoint eligibility, collateral state, and clean rerun. Negative controls pin current cache/concurrency/warming/container/cancellation behavior and prove legacy/corrupt envelopes cause calls rather than reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Plan review executes selected discovery work through the shared typed kernel while preserving current YAML topology, facet packing, fallback ladder, centrality budget, bounded concurrency, and cache warming.
- [x] Container, prerequisite, remediation, deterministic-floor, relation-snapshot, cancellation, and signing paths retain their current observable contracts when no approved delta applies.
- [x] A failed local unit cannot serialize as a clean checkpoint; earlier successes survive, independent work continues, dependents skip, and the final `BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE`/advisory-only `PASS` policy matches the approved rule.
- [x] The new checkpoint key changes when any material, code/ref, policy, prompt, contract, model/mode, topology, context, dependency, or namespace input changes; corrupt and legacy entries produce zero reuse.
- [x] Only content-identical success/resume envelopes seed reuse, while failed, cancelled, skipped, and budget-shed units remain missing and callable on a later run.
- [x] The reducer-ignored review journal stores the safe versioned trace, while `review-plan` and `review-plan --status` outputs contain only their established end-result fields.
- [x] Shadow tests use the same observed calls and find no unapproved selection, order, context, model, budget, usage, cache, checkpoint, or verdict differences.
